# Single source of truth

Before creating or changing a durable artifact, find its declared owner in the
project source catalogue and the sources named by the task. Edit that owner and
link to it elsewhere.

The producing system owns live facts: the task tracker owns ticket state, code
owns implemented behavior, analytics owns observed results, and company-context
owns company facts and work ownership. A source document defines meaning; a
report cites that definition instead of creating another one.

Name disagreeing sources, the proposed owner and the reason. Do not choose
silently. Reconcile within the task's authority, or record the conflict for its
owner and continue independent work. Missing access is a named limit, not a
reason to invent a replacement source.

A required generated projection names its canonical source, source revision and
regeneration command. Edit its source and regenerate it. Skills link to source
documents; indexes and routers link to the owning procedure rather than
repeating it.

When an approved replacement takes over, repoint live consumers together and
retire competing editable copies. Preserve historical evidence as history. An
unpublished staging copy is not a second live owner and must say so explicitly.
